p: Escape rooms reward teamwork more than brainpower. The best teams talk constantly, shouting out every clue, number and odd-looking object they find, even if it doesn't seem important. Keep found items in one place so nothing gets lost, and if you're stuck on a puzzle for more than a few minutes, let a fresh pair of eyes have a go. Don't be too proud to ask for a hint if the game allows it; it's far better than spending half your time staring at the same lock.

Think about your team when you book. Smaller groups give everyone more to do, while bigger ones bring more brains but can get a bit chaotic. If you've got a large party, splitting into rival teams across different rooms can add a brilliant competitive edge. It's a good idea to check age guidance for younger players when booking, and turning up a little early gives time for the briefing.

Fountainbridge has plenty to explore once you're out. Edinburgh Printmakers, in the restored former North British Rubber Company building at Castle Mills, has a gallery, shop and café. The Union Canal towpath leads west towards Harrison Park and beyond for a longer walk or cycle. The Usher Hall and the Royal Lyceum Theatre are close by on Lothian Road and Grindlay Street, and the Meadows, a big open park to the south, is lovely for a stroll before heading back to the Old Town. Perfect for walking off the adrenaline.
